title: Iberian and Cosenza local Missal witnesses, a Roman Latin lay-book comparison, and a deferred Albanian control

traditions.label: Barcelona local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1498 Barcelona Missal and its surviving fragment, not a complete diocesan recension.
traditions.coverage_note: The extant copy is fragmentary and original pages have not been independently collated here.

traditions.label: Salamanca local Mass books
traditions.scope: The 1533 Missale Salmanticense as an identified local printed book.
traditions.coverage_note: Its title reports correction and augmentation, but the relevant predecessor and decree remain uninspected.

traditions.label: Seville local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1565 Missale Hispalense, including its inspected title and printer's preface.
traditions.coverage_note: The printer's correction claim is not a component-level comparison or a normative decree.

traditions.label: Toledo Roman-type local Mass books
traditions.scope: The identified 1551 Roman-type Toledo Missal, kept separate from the Hispano-Mozarabic books.
traditions.coverage_note: Its title describes additions; original pages and predecessor comparison are uninspected.

traditions.label: Cosenza local Mass books
traditions.scope: The catalogue-identified Missale Cosentinum of 1549 and its indexed Mass components.
traditions.coverage_note: A local title and component inventory do not establish an ancient Gallican ancestry or a complete textual state.

traditions.label: Roman Latin Ordinary in identified lay books
traditions.scope: Native Latin columns in the 1861 Cummiskey lay missal as a Roman comparison witness only.
traditions.coverage_note: The English translation's independent history and any claim of an altar-book recension are outside this stage.

traditions.label: Buzuku Albanian historical witness control
traditions.scope: Identity and reception questions for the 1555 Albanian mixed liturgical book; independent historical translation history is deferred.
traditions.coverage_note: No original-language Roman book state or distinct Roman recension is admitted from this witness.

sources.title: Usuarium 48, Missale Barcinonense
sources.inspection: Read the original-title, 1498 date, printer, Barcelona Inc. 46-Fol. holding, fragment notice, and indexed Ordinary, Canon and local sanctoral entries.
sources.limitations: The catalogue describes a fragment surviving from Holy Saturday to 25 January; original leaves, imprint and omitted extent were not directly checked.

sources.title: Usuarium 55, Missale Salmanticense
sources.inspection: Read the 1533 bibliographic fields, title's claim of correction and augmentation, BG/18686 holding, and contents locations for episcopal front matter, temporal, Canon and colophon.
sources.limitations: The catalogue transcribes the title and indexes a decree; original title, decree, colophon and predecessor text were not inspected.

sources.title: Usuarium 57, Missale Hispalense
sources.inspection: Read the 1565 bibliographic fields, A Res. 10/1/06 holding and indexed printer's preface, temporal, Ordinary, Canon, sanctoral and colophon locations.
sources.limitations: The indexed page labelled decree begins with the printer's name; the catalogue label is not evidence of episcopal promulgation.

sources.title: Missale Hispalense, Seville 1565 original facsimile
sources.inspection: Existing reviewed acquisition inspected original PDF pages 13 and 16: title and printer's preface, including its claim of correction; the repository source record identifies this exact facsimile.
sources.limitations: Only named front pages have been inspected; no original predecessor, complete body collation or competent-authority act is established.

sources.title: Usuarium 60, Missale Toletanum
sources.inspection: Read the 1551 bibliographic fields, BM Lyon SJ L 013/14 holding, Roman-type Toledo warning, title's additions claim, and indexed Mass sections and colophon.
sources.limitations: The Roman-type classification is the catalogue's; original title, appended rites, authorization and predecessor text were not checked directly.

sources.title: Usuarium 5816, Missale Cosentinum
sources.inspection: Read the local title, 1549 age, BL Legg88 holding, and indexed calendar, Ordinary, Canon, temporal, sanctoral and votive Mass components.
sources.limitations: The catalogue's printer authority gives Peter Liechtenstein active 1497–1528 despite a 1549 book date; inspect the actual imprint and succession before assigning the printing firm. No whole-text collation was made.

sources.title: Cummiskey 1861 Roman Missal for the laity, registered Latin Ordinary artifacts
sources.inspection: Read the repository's canonical Philadelphia 1861 edition manifest and six pre-existing native Latin Ordinary, Canon and preface artifact manifests; the earlier review verified the retained bytes against all six registered hashes and lengths.
sources.limitations: The exact remote Google scan behind the landing page was not acquired in this pass; only the retained native Latin component transcriptions and edition identity support this stage.

sources.title: Biblioteka Kombëtare e Shqipërisë, Buzuku Meshari facsimile record 92035
sources.inspection: The existing reviewed research record read the facsimile catalogue heading and notes on the bracketed 1555 year, incomplete Vatican exemplar, missing leaves and undated handwritten Latin-source attribution.
sources.limitations: The catalogue describes a derivative facsimile, not a directly collated surviving book; its Latin-source note is undated and does not establish a specific exemplar or approval.

stages.label: 1498 Barcelona Missal fragment
stages.scope: Identity of a local Missal printing and indexed components surviving in a fragment.
stages.witness_label: Missale Barcinonense, Biblioteca de Catalunya Inc. 46-Fol.
stages.summary: The catalogue identifies a 1498 Missal for the Barcelona church and warns that the surviving copy begins at Holy Saturday.

evidence.locus: bibliographic fields, Remark and Contents pp. 143–151
evidence.claim: A dated local Missal fragment contains indexed Ordinary, Canon and local sanctoral material.

stages.limitations: The publication date is catalogue reported; neither missing earlier leaves nor any subsequent local use is reconstructed.
stages.reception: The title identifies intended Barcelona church use; actual local adoption and jurisdictional duration are unverified.

stages.label: 1533 Salamanca Missal print
stages.scope: Identity of a 1533 local Missal; title's correction claim is reported without a collated predecessor.
stages.summary: The catalogue records the 1533 Salamanca Missal and transcribes a title claiming correction and added Masses and priestly instructions.

evidence.locus: Original title, Age, holding and Contents pp. 5–7, 45, 355, 609
evidence.claim: The identified printing has a local title and indexed Mass-book components; its self-description claims improvement.

stages.limitations: No specific before and after readings or episcopal decree text have been inspected, so a substantive revision and effective date remain open.
stages.reception: The book addresses Salamanca church use; actual extent of reception is not independently documented.

stages.label: 1551 Roman-type Toledo Missal print
stages.scope: Identity of one Roman-type Toledo local Missal, not the Hispano-Mozarabic Missale mixtum.
stages.witness_label: Missale Toletanum, BM Lyon SJ L 013/14
stages.summary: The inspected catalogue identifies the 1551 Toledo book as Roman type and indexes its local Mass sections.

evidence.claim: The source explicitly distinguishes the Roman-type Toledo witness from the Mozarabic Missal and locates its Mass and rubric sections.

stages.limitations: The title's stated additions have no checked predecessor comparison; no competent act or complete text is established.
stages.reception: Local title and Roman-type classification are bibliographic evidence, not proof of a dated diocesan adoption.

stages.label: 1565 Seville Missal print
stages.scope: One Seville local Missal printing with inspected original title and printer's prefatory correction claim.
stages.witness_label: Missale Hispalense, BU Sevilla A Res. 10/1/06
stages.summary: Original title and printer's preface identify the local 1565 book and report correction; indexed contents locate its Mass sections.

evidence.claim: The original front pages name the local book and carry a printer's reported correction claim.
The catalogue dates and indexes the specific surviving copy.

stages.limitations: The preface is a printer's address, not a demonstrated episcopal decree; no exact corrected readings or predecessor have been collated.
stages.reception: The title names Seville church custom; no independent dated mandate or full diocesan use span is established.

stages.label: 1549 Cosenza Missal print
stages.scope: Identity of an indexed Cosenza local Missal printing and its Mass-book components.
stages.summary: Usuarium catalogues a 1549 Cosenza Missal with local title and indexed Ordinary, Canon and Mass sections.

evidence.locus: Original title, Age, BL Legg88 holding and Contents pp. 14–34, 305–314, 440
evidence.claim: The source identifies a dated local Missal and its indexed Eucharistic components.

stages.limitations: The printer attribution conflicts with the catalogue's own activity dates and requires original imprint inspection; named Gallic custom and scholarly Burchard comparison do not establish whole-book ancestry.
stages.reception: The title describes Cosenza church custom; actual local authorization and period of use remain unverified.

stages.label: 1861 Cummiskey lay-book Latin Ordinary
stages.scope: Only the book's own Latin Ordinary, Canon and preface columns, retained as partial Roman Latin comparison material.
stages.witness_label: Cummiskey 1861 Philadelphia first revised lay missal
stages.summary: A dated lay book preserves native Latin Ordinary and Canon columns that can be compared with Roman altar books.

evidence.locus: canonical 1861 edition manifest; six registered Latin component artifacts
evidence.claim: The identified first revised edition and checked Latin component transcriptions support a bounded comparison witness.

stages.limitations: The retained columns are not a complete altar missal or proof of a distinct normative Roman recension; exact remote scan remains unresolved.
stages.reception: The title reports a Philadelphia bishop's approbation of a lay book; it does not grant authorization to celebrate from this edition.

gaps.missing: Original title and colophon checks, complete extent of the fragment, earlier and later Barcelona Mass books, local authority and direct text comparison.
gaps.next_source: Inspect Biblioteca de Catalunya Inc. 46-Fol. images and find dated Barcelona missals for component-level collation.
gaps.consequence: The catalogue's publication year does not date adoption or establish a revision sequence.

gaps.missing: Original title, bishop's front matter, colophon, claimed corrected readings and predecessor or successor witnesses.
gaps.next_source: Read BU Salamanca BG/18686 original pages 5, 7 and 609 and collate matching Mass components against an earlier Salmanticense.
gaps.consequence: The title's repair claim cannot yet be promoted to a documented substantive transition or effective date.

gaps.missing: A named predecessor, exact corrected Mass readings, full text and competent-authority permission or use record.
gaps.next_source: Collate the acquired 1565 original against an earlier Hispalense at named Ordinary and proper loci; inspect authority leaves separately from the printer's preface.
gaps.consequence: The correction notice supports a research lead, not a reform edge or universal-use claim.

gaps.missing: Original title and appended rite pages, added sanctoral Mass readings, local authorization and a Roman-type Toledo predecessor.
gaps.next_source: Inspect BM Lyon SJ L 013/14 or linked original facsimile, then compare Toledo Roman-type books without using Mozarabic volumes as predecessors.
gaps.consequence: Neither the word mixtum nor a reported addition proves Hispanic-rite ancestry or a dated revision.

gaps.missing: Original imprint resolution, complete local text, earlier/later Cosenza witnesses, Burchard component loci and adoption evidence.
gaps.next_source: Inspect BL London Legg88 facsimile or original and compare Legg's cited components with an identified donor book, then trace episcopal records.
gaps.consequence: The catalogue date and Gallic title wording do not establish ancient descent or a local reform.

gaps.missing: Exact remote scan verification of retained Latin columns, complete Roman exemplar identification and component-level comparison beyond the partial artifacts.
gaps.next_source: Acquire the exact Philadelphia 1861 scan and compare its Latin columns at named loci with an edition-identified Roman altar Missal.
gaps.consequence: A lay publication and partial Latin transcription cannot count as a new normative Roman version or complete service-book text.

gaps.missing: Direct collation of the incomplete Vatican original or authorized facsimile, its Mass components and Latin exemplars, contemporary permission and actual liturgical use.
gaps.next_source: Inspect Vatican R.G. Liturgia III, 194 and an authenticated facsimile with leaf-loss map; examine original Mass loci and contemporary diocesan records.
gaps.consequence: An Albanian mixed liturgical witness remains identifiable, but its independent translation history is deferred and it cannot supply a Roman source recension or book-state stage here.
